brief: Limit threads to 1. NO YT community posts (no YT posts, no carousels). Add 3 YouTube community QUIZZES drawn from the stream (schema in schedule-tweets/data/yt-quizzes.json: question, 2-4 options each 65 chars max, exactly one correct, short explanation). Make 3 of the X tweets about Kaspa and/or KRC20 tokens.

fact_check.claim: 'now it's at 83% there's going to be a pause on our rate' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified and current. CME FedWatch for the October 27-28 FOMC on Friday October 16, 2026: 83.9% hold at 3.75% to 4.00%, 16.1% for a 25 bp hike (down from 27.7% Thursday after PPI and a brief move toward 44% Wednesday after CPI). Copy says '84% chance of pausing'. Chair Warsh's Bangkok remarks did not revive hike bets.

fact_check.claim: 'worse than expected PPI readings... the day before we got worse than expected CPI readings' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified. September 2026 PPI (released October 15): 6.3% year over year vs 5.3% expected, core 5.0% vs 4.4%, headline +1.3% month over month; Cointelegraph headlines it as the biggest PPI gain in over four years, so copy says 'the hottest PPI print in over four years'. September CPI (October 14): 3.7% year over year, hotter than expected (verified in the downtober ledger from CNBC). Copy uses 3.7% and 6.3%.

fact_check.claim: 'the low is 79 six. So I went below 80 K in those two hours... it closed as a green candle' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified. Bitcoin printed an intraday low of about $79,800 after the PPI release on October 15 and rebounded to about $82,000 to $83,000 the same day (about $930M liquidated market-wide). The 'about two hours' duration is Mike's read of his hourly chart and is kept as his statement. Current price about $81,300 (CoinDesk/CoinGecko, October 16).

fact_check.claim: 'the NASDAQ closed the week down 5.5%. The lowest weekly decline since April of 2025. And it is now 7% below its high from just 10 days ago' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified for the Nasdaq 100 (Bloomberg: 5.5% weekly loss, worst week since the April 2025 tariff turmoil); the Nasdaq Composite lost about 4.5% to 5%. Copy names the Nasdaq 100. The '7% below its high' detail could not be confirmed and is not used.

fact_check.claim: 'oil climbs to 110... bread oil surges, $111' (transcript; 'bread' = Brent)
fact_check.verdict: verified. Brent crude around $110 a barrel, its highest since May 2026; WTI $101.71 on October 16. Copy says 'Brent oil near $110'.

fact_check.claim: 'U.S. deficit jumps 12% to nearly 2 trillion' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified. Treasury's final fiscal 2026 tally (October 16): $1.992 trillion, up from $1.775 trillion in fiscal 2025 (about 12%), third largest on record, net interest above $1 trillion. Copy says 'a $2 trillion deficit, up 12% in one year'.

fact_check.claim: 'the bottom was in June 30th, which is the exact end of quarter two' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified. Bitcoin's 2026 low printed on June 30: about $58,379 (KuCoin), just under $59,000 (CoinDesk), about 53% below the $126,198 all-time high of October 6, 2025 (Coinbase daily candles put the wick at about $57.7K on July 1 UTC, the same session). Copy says 'about $58K on June 30, about 53% off the top'.

fact_check.claim: 'people are going to front run the supposed prophesied bottom in October. And we're going to start going up in September, which is exactly what we did' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified. Bitcoin rebounded about 45% from the June low by late September and traded about $85,300 to $85,450 around the October 6 anniversary of the high. Copy says 'about 45% off the June low to about $85K by late September'.

fact_check.claim: 'I had been saying since like August of last year... a really really disappointing local top... dump in January... crypto winter for a quarter or two' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: Mike's own statement of his prior calls (his streams, Discord and Telegram); the thread presents them as his calls and checks them against verified market facts (top October 6, 2025 at $126,198; low June 30, 2026). The 'January dump' is written as his call, not as a measured January figure. 'Then everybody front-running the October bottom' and the '10% odds of a new bottom months after October' are likewise his own stated probabilities from July and August.

fact_check.claim: 'Bloomberg intelligence strategist Micah McClone warns Bitcoin could fall to under $10,000, particularly if the US stock market suffers a 20% drawdown' (transcript; = Mike McGlone)
fact_check.verdict: verified (McGlone's conditional scenario: BTC toward $10,000 on a prolonged 20% S&P 500 drawdown, framed as a stress case not a forecast; coverage dated September 13 and October 16, 2026). Not drafted: dark-register BTC-to-$10K content stays off the Kaspa-weighted lineup this batch and would need the 2008-analogy framing that invites the wrong read.

fact_check.claim: 'Bitcoin goes down by like 85%, one bull run, then 84%... then 73%... this particular bear market the drawdown was like 53%' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: approximately right (historical peak-to-trough drawdowns about 93% in 2011, 85% to 86% in 2014-15, 84% in 2018, 77% in 2022, about 53% in 2025-26). Only the 53% figure is used in copy.

fact_check.claim: 'we don't know until it gets above the 50 week moving average... we're riding on the 50 day' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: kept as Mike's framework (quiz 2: the 50-week SMA is his bull-run confirmation level; the 50-day is short-term support). No price level for either average is quoted in copy.

fact_check.claim: 'Developers now have native tools on Kaspa that simply didn't exist before. Thanks to Covenants and a move forward to KCC 20... the ecosystem works on bridging KRC20 to KCC20' (transcript, read off a Kaspa ecosystem post)
fact_check.verdict: verified. Covenants activated on Kaspa mainnet with the Toccata upgrade at DAA score 474,165,565, which arrived about June 30, 2026 (1,078 active covenant IDs as of October 6). KCC-20, the covenant-native fungible token standard, is still Draft (a Last Call proposal is open); KCC-1 and KCC-2 reached Last Call October 1. KaspaCom is reported to be building a one-way bridge moving KRC20 and Kaspa L2 tokens onto KCC-20. Copy: 'Covenants have been live on Kaspa mainnet since the end of June', 'KCC-20 token standard is in draft', 'the ecosystem is working on bridging KRC20 tokens over to it'. KRC20 itself went live on Kaspa mainnet September 15, 2024 (quiz 1).

fact_check.claim: 'Kaspa rocket.fun... beta on Kaspa testnet... Testnet 10' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: verified from the project's own site only (self-reported): 'KaspaRocket is currently in beta testing on Kaspa Testnet-10', a memecoin launchpad, 'Fair launch, no pre-sale, no team allocation', test KAS from the TN10 faucet. No independent coverage, so copy keeps it generic ('a fair-launch memecoin launchpad is in beta on testnet-10') and never names the product.

fact_check.claim: 'slippy is a KRC 20 token that launched this year. It wasn't from the KRC 20 season' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: CORRECTED, no content drafted. The Kasplex KRC20 API shows SLIPPY deployed 2025-07-13 (last year, after the 2024 KRC20 season, so 'not from the season' is right but 'this year' is not), 260 holders, mint finished. A reference file (slippy.png) exists, but the claim as spoken is wrong and the token is too small to carry a tweet.

fact_check.claim: Kaspa price (not stated on stream; copy needs the current level)
fact_check.verdict: current: about $0.036 (Bybit $0.03636, Coinbase $0.03628 on October 17, 2026), market cap about $1.01B, about 82% under the 20.7-cent all-time high. Copy says 'about 3.6 cents', 'under 4 cents', 'roughly a $1B market cap'.

fact_check.claim: 'How's Toshi doing? $45 million... meme season comes probably an easy 10 X on Toshi' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: updated: TOSHI market cap about $46.4M (CoinGecko; Kraken/Blockworks about $43M to $44M, Coinbase about $53M), 95% below its all-time high. Copy says 'about a $46M market cap' and does not quote a multiple.

fact_check.claim: 'turbo could 10 X to all time high' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: roughly right but understated: TURBO about $0.0009, market cap about $62M, 93.7% below its all-time high of $0.01432 (about 16x). Not used as a number; Turbo is named only in poll options.

fact_check.claim: 'the gas fees were insane... you want to cash out $30 and you have to pay $20... people paying like $100 in gas fees' (transcript, Ethereum)
fact_check.verdict: NOT verified, dropped. Ethereum trackers show the base fee near record lows in October 2026 (about 0.07 gwei, cents per transfer); Mike's anecdote is a specific token/moment that cannot be reproduced. No Ethereum gas content drafted.

fact_check.claim: Neptune privacy coin ($XNT, SafeTrade), Bike Tyson, Hellhound, Crawl Scan, 'Proof of War' coins, Tensor cash, Tick coin, 'my math theory' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: unverified micro-caps and chat mentions, skipped; Mike himself passed on Neptune ('better plays than Neptune') and on the new memes. No content drafted.

fact_check.claim: Citi restricting AI agents from accounts (FT); 'open call' agent charging $4,000 (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: off-lineup AI tangent, not researched, no content drafted.

fact_check.claim: Flying car / DeLorean / OJ Simpson / John Candy / Crypto Wendy videos; Trump 'economy has never been stronger' (transcript)
fact_check.verdict: personal and political tangents (persona avoid_in_drafts), skipped. Mike can post these himself.

The calls Mike made from August 2025 onward, checked against what happened: a disappointing local top ($126K, October 6, 2025), a January dump into a crypto winter of a quarter or two (low about $58K on June 30, the last day of Q2), the September front-run of the prophesied October bottom (about 45% off the low to about $85K), the zombies buying the PPI-day red candle under $80K back to a green close, and the one scenario he does not want to be right about (a new bottom months after October) with CPI 3.7%, PPI 6.3%, oil near $110, a $2T deficit and an 84% pause priced for October 28. Standalone thread (no YT post this batch per the brief).

tweets.text:
Was I right?

Last August I laid out the whole year in advance: a disappointing local top, a January dump, a crypto winter lasting a quarter or two, then everybody front-running the October bottom.

Here is how it actually played out...

The disappointing top.

Bitcoin ($BTC) peaked at about $126K on October 6, 2025, and that was it. No blow-off, no $200K, just a top that left everybody unsatisfied.

Exactly the setup I described.

The dump and the winter.

I said they would get pissed off, dump in January, and hand us a crypto winter for a quarter or two.

The low printed June 30 at about $58K, about 53% off the top. June 30 is the last day of Q2. Two quarters, to the day.

The front-run.

Through July and August I said people would front-run the prophesied October bottom and we would start going up in September.

Bitcoin ran about 45% off the June low to about $85K by late September. Right on schedule.

The October candles.

I said the four-year cycle zombies would not let red candles run in October. PPI day: Bitcoin under $80K for about two hours, then bought straight back up to a green close.

On the hottest PPI print in over four years.

Now the part I do NOT want to be right about.

Back in August I gave 10% odds to a new bottom printing months after October. CPI 3.7%, PPI 6.3%, oil near $110, a $2T deficit, and an 84% pause priced in for October 28.

We need good news, and we need it fast.

Kaspa Maxis did not wait for an October bottom; we stacked $KAS through the summer and we are still stacking.

So tell me: is the bottom behind us, or does a new one print months after October?

Follow me for the calls before they happen 🔥
